method: Page fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Every claim is verbatim-checked against that file with scripts/verify.py. Prose paraphrases; source_text stays verbatim. NOTE: the page marks red flag features by COLOUR ('Red flag features in Red'), which does not survive text extraction, so the red flag set could not be isolated and is recorded as input_unavailable rather than guessed. Source last updated July 2019, seven years before retrieval, and it carries desmopressin doses.

claims.claim: Night continence is a normal developmental process with a strong genetic tendency
claims.source_text: Attaining night time continence is a normal developmental process, with significant age variation. There is a strong genetic tendency to bedwetting

claims.claim: Age expectations and prevalence at 4 and 6 years
claims.source_text: bladder control and coordination usually occurs by 4 years of age, however night-time … bladder control typically takes longer and is not expected until a child is 5-7 … years old. At 4 years of age, nearly 1 in 3 children wets … the bed, but this falls to about 1 in 10 by age 6

claims.claim: Treatment usually not started before age 6
claims.source_text: Enuresis is common and generally causes no lasting problems. Typically treatment is not started before age 6 years, as there is a high rate of spontaneous resolution

claims.claim: Pathogenesis mechanisms
claims.source_text: The pathogenesis involves several possible mechanisms including nocturnal polyuria, detrusor overactivity and an increased arousal threshold

claims.claim: Treatment threshold is social interference
claims.source_text: For most children, enuresis is only seen as a problem when it interferes with their ability to socialise with friends (for example overnight stays or school camps). If the enuresis is infrequent and/or not distressing to the child or parents, treatment is not

claims.claim: Most children have no underlying problem but suffer shame
claims.source_text: Most children who wet the bed have no significant underlying physical or emotional problems. However, many will feel embarrassed or ashamed and suffer from decreased self-esteem, particularly as the child gets older

claims.claim: Monosymptomatic enuresis definition
claims.source_text: Monosymptomatic enuresis (MSE) is defined as enuresis without any other lower urinary tract symptoms or history of bladder dysfunction

claims.claim: Daytime symptoms require a different approach and may be treated first
claims.source_text: The presence of daytime, lower urinary tract symptoms requires a different approach … If daytime symptoms predominate, consider treating before bedwetting

claims.claim: History focuses on voiding habits
claims.source_text: Much of the history should focus … on voiding habits

claims.claim: Acute onset may indicate systemic illness
claims.source_text: Onset of bedwetting (if … last few days to weeks - consider whether this is a presentation of systemic illness)

claims.claim: Six months of prior dryness and secondary enuresis referral
claims.source_text: Has the child previously been dry at night without assistance for 6 months? … The presence of unexplained persistent … secondary enuresis despite adequate management should prompt specialist referral

claims.claim: Daytime symptom checklist
claims.source_text: Presence of day-time symptoms (frequency, urgency, polyuria, dysuria/recurrent … poor urinary stream/straining, leakage)

claims.claim: Bowel habit, sleep and comorbidity history
claims.source_text: Bowel habit (constipation/soiling) … Sleeping arrangements and routine (including own bed/bedroom, snoring and disturbed sleep) … developmental or behavioural problems, diabetes mellitus or sleep apnoea

claims.claim: Social history includes family capacity and vulnerability
claims.source_text: family capacity and motivation to engage in treatment, social difficulties (vulnerable child/family)

claims.claim: Examination items including spine
claims.source_text: Height, weight, BP - poor growth / loss of weight / … Abdomen - distended bladder, faecal mass … Lower Back/Spine - exclude occult spinal dysraphism or tethered cord (asymmetric/deviation of gluteal cleft) … Assessment of lower limb neurology

claims.claim: Urinalysis not required in primary enuresis
claims.source_text: Dipstick urinalysis is not required in primary enuresis. Consider if red flags apparent. Further imaging or blood tests are not routinely recommended in enuresis

claims.claim: Constipation must be managed first
claims.source_text: Constipation, if present, should be adequately managed before addressing enuresis

claims.claim: Encourage regular fluids and toileting
claims.source_text: Encourage regular fluids and toileting throughout the day (eg during school break times) and just before bedtime

claims.claim: Advise against fluid restriction but eliminate evening caffeine
claims.source_text: Advise against fluid restriction, but eliminate caffeinated beverages in the evening

claims.claim: Explain normal bladder function and that it is common
claims.source_text: Advise on normal bladder function and the pathogenesis of enuresis, including the genetic tendency. Also, that this is a common problem effecting their peer group and they should not be embarrassed

claims.claim: Both parent and child must be motivated
claims.source_text: Both parent and child must be motivated before starting behavioural interventions

claims.claim: Alarm therapy is the most effective modality over 6 years
claims.source_text: Alarm therapy is the most effective treatment modality available in children older than 6 years of age, but requires motivation of both child and parent

claims.claim: Alarms have better long-term success than medication
claims.source_text: Considered the most useful and successful initial way to treat bedwetting - good long-term success and fewer relapses than medication

claims.claim: Alarms take 6 to 8 weeks and are recommended from 6-7 years
claims.source_text: it may take 6-8 weeks … to work … Generally recommended in children from 6-7 … years of age, depending on their physical ability, maturity and motivation

claims.claim: Alarms are hired from pharmacies and continence services
claims.source_text: Bedwetting alarms are available for hire from selected pharmacies, community continence services, tertiary centres, and private practitioners. The Continence Foundation of Australia has a list of

claims.claim: Intellectual and hearing impairment do not preclude alarm therapy
claims.source_text: Mild to moderate intellectual impairment does not preclude treatment and in hearing impaired children consider using a vibrating alarm

claims.claim: Carer emotional state is a contraindication to alarm therapy
claims.source_text: Not suitable if the carer is experiencing emotional difficulty, expressing anger or blame toward the child, or is unlikely to cope with the additional burden of a bedwetting alarm and sleep disruption in the household

claims.claim: The child must be fully awake during the process
claims.source_text: Children should be 'in charge' of their alarm and may need to be woken initially to turn the alarm off themselves. It is critical for success of alarm therapy that the child is fully awake during the process of going to the bathroom

claims.claim: Reward the behaviour not the dry night
claims.source_text: Reward systems can be useful during alarm therapy to reward behaviours such as waking or going to the toilet when the alarm goes off (Not for dry nights per se)

claims.claim: Alarm response timelines
claims.source_text: If a child is showing early signs of response after 4 weeks, continue treatment until 2 weeks of uninterrupted dry nights are achieved … Discontinue treatment if no early signs of response within 4 weeks … incomplete dryness after 3 months, reconsider if ongoing treatment is appropriate or a further trial of the alarm in 3-6 months

claims.claim: Overlearning method
claims.source_text: Once dryness is achieved for 2 weeks or more, consider introducing “overlearning” - to over condition the bladder. Encourage the child to drink extra fluids in the hour before bedtime, providing a greater challenge to remaining dry, which may reduce the rate of relapse

claims.claim: Tricyclics are no longer recommended
claims.source_text: Tricyclic medications are no longer recommended. They are less effective than other therapies and have a higher risk of adverse events

claims.claim: Desmopressin indications
claims.source_text: alarm therapy has failed or is not suitable … if rapid onset/short-term improvement is a priority of treatment

claims.claim: Desmopressin relapse rate on withdrawal
claims.source_text: Relapse rates are high when withdrawn, (60-70 percent)

claims.claim: Desmopressin sublingual and oral dosing
claims.source_text: 6 years, sublingual, initially 120 micrograms at bedtime; if needed, after 1-2 weeks increase to a maximum of 240 micrograms at bedtime … 6 years, oral, initially 200 micrograms at bedtime; if needed, increase to 400 micrograms at bedtime

claims.claim: Intranasal route not recommended due to hyponatraemia
claims.source_text: route is not recommended due to higher risk of hyponatraemia

claims.claim: Fluid restriction window and contraindication
claims.source_text: Restrict fluid from 1 hour before the dose until at least 8 hours after the dose. Desmopressin is contraindicated for children who can't

claims.claim: Assess at 4 weeks and withdraw every 3 months
claims.source_text: Assess response after 4 weeks to determine continuation of treatment (if no response consider cessation). … Withdraw for at least 1 week every 3 months to assess for relapse and ongoing need for medication

claims.claim: Lifting and waking do not promote long-term dryness
claims.source_text: Neither lifting (carrying a child to the toilet with an effort not to wake them) nor waking and walking the child to the toilet will promote long-term dryness

claims.claim: Self-instigated waking may be useful
claims.source_text: Waking a child by parents or carers, either regularly or randomly, is only a short-term method of managing bedwetting. A young person who self-instigates waking (using a mobile phone alarm or an alarm clock) may be a useful strategy

claims.claim: Referral triggers
claims.source_text: Persistent enuresis with failure of an enuresis alarm … Day-time enuresis or combined day/night enuresis after exclusion or treatment of a UTI and constipation … History of recurrent urinary tract infections … Comorbidities such as type 1 diabetes, physical or neurological problems … Substantial psychological or behavioural problems (consider mental health referral, paediatrician and/or child protection services if significant concern exists)
